summary: A feature piece on Hollywood families who keep traditions and legacies alive, set in September 2023. It profiles the Ferguson, Nguyen, Weiss, Lopez, Silver and Emerson families, each with a ritual, celebration, or creative practice that connects past and future. The article argues that these personal narratives are an integral part of Hollywood beyond its glitzy facade.
one_line: Profiles of six Hollywood families (Ferguson, Nguyen, Weiss, Lopez, Silver, Emerson) and the traditions that carry their legacies forward in September 2023.
key_facts: The Ferguson family has held Sunday dinners since 1980, started by Marjorie and Bartholomew Ferguson to stay close.

Marjorie Ferguson makes a roast chicken dinner and believes eating together keeps the extended family's spirit alive (the article says Friday in one place, despite calling the tradition Sunday dinners).
The Nguyen family's 40th family-held Mid-Autumn Festival is set for September 18, 2023, honoring their Vietnamese roots.
Tran Nguyen, the family patriarch, said: "When we left Saigon we brought with us only our traditions."
The Weiss family marks the release of their latest blockbuster at the Egyptian Theatre on September 10, 2023, combined with a family reunion.
The Weiss family gathers in the loft above their famed costume shop, where elders recount their escape from war-ravaged Europe.
Simon Weiss says: "Our legacy lives on in every outfit we've created."
The Lopez family is painting a mural on a local community center wall in East Hollywood, with family roots there dating to the 1960s.
Abuela Carmen and little Luis of the Lopez family contribute to the mural, which is tied to September 15, 2023.
The Silver family theatre troupe has performed since 1923, and the article says September 2023 marks their 85th year at their local playhouse.
Matriarch Vivian Silver calls each performance "a living memorial of those who preceded us".
The Emerson family documents milestones on Super 8 film and will premiere a new feature-length film on September 29, 2023, including footage from a trip around Europe.
Henry Emerson hosts surprise outdoor screenings of family films at his Hollywood Hills home and calls it "our own star on Hollywood heritage's walk of fame".
